summary: Across 4 K, 150 K and 295 K the dominant change is not a phonon shift but the excitation-energy dependence of the Raman intensities, which moves with temperature. At matched laser energies the A1g intensity falls by about 2 decades from 4 K to 295 K at 587 nm and by about 1.5 decades at 599 nm, but rises at 623/624 nm. The resonance maximum moves from at least 2.11 eV (4 K) to about 2.05 eV (150 K) to about 2.01 eV (295 K). The low-temperature luminescence background is large (up to 9e4 counts at 4 K, 611 nm) and falls on warming at 587–611 nm, but it is weak at 4 K and strongest at 295 K for 623/624 nm. The separation Δ = ω(A1g) − ω(E2g) is 60.9 ± 0.3 cm⁻¹ in all 12 spectra and shows no temperature dependence within about ±0.3 cm⁻¹, which suggests the same layer number and no large change in strain or doping over the range. Absolute phonon frequencies cannot be used to infer a temperature coefficient here: they co-shift with the Si band by 1–3 cm⁻¹ between runs and laser settings, which points to axis calibration rather than sample physics. Linewidths are at or near the instrument resolution and show no resolvable narrowing on cooling. The low-shift edge near 135–165 cm⁻¹ and a 146–147 cm⁻¹ feature on it are filter/window artifacts, so interlayer modes and LA(M) are not accessible.

observations.finding: At matched laser energies the A1g intensity depends on temperature in the opposite direction on either side of the resonance. It falls by about 2 decades from 4 K to 295 K at 587 nm and about 1.5 decades at 599 nm, but rises from 4 K to 295 K at 611 nm (peak near 150 K) and at 623/624 nm.
observations.evidence: Integrated A1g area (Lorentzian amp*pi*FWHM/2, 2 Lorentzians on the E2g window, Lorentzian on A1g, quadratic baseline): 587 nm 1.09e6 (4K) / 1.20e5 (150K) / 5.0e3 (295K); 599 nm 8.4e5 / 3.4e5 / 2.4e4 (598.8 nm); 611 nm 3.0e5 / 3.5e5 / 1.1e5 (610.3 nm); 623/624 nm 2.7e4 (622.7 nm) / 3.7e4 (623.5 nm) / 9.6e4 (624.0 nm). E2g areas follow the same pattern.

observations.finding: The resonance maximum of the A1g intensity moves to lower laser energy on warming. At 4 K the intensity is monotonic with a maximum at the highest laser energy (2.11 eV, so the resonance is at or above 2.11 eV). The estimated maximum is about 2.05 eV at 150 K and about 2.01 eV at 295 K.
observations.evidence: Parabolic estimate through ln(A1g area) vs laser energy: 150 K ≈ 2.048 eV (flat between 2.03 and 2.07 eV); 295 K ≈ 2.013 eV. Only four laser energies per temperature, so the uncertainty is about ±0.03 eV.
observations.source: Interpretation of the measured resonance profile; magnitude of the A-exciton temperature shift in WS2 from Wang et al., Rev. Mod. Phys. 90, 021001 (2018), exciton-energy summary (from memory, verify).

observations.finding: The broad luminescence-type background, which dominates the raw 4 K spectra, is strongly laser- and temperature-dependent. At 587–611 nm it falls on warming, but at 623/624 nm it rises on warming.
observations.evidence: Median counts at 240–260 cm⁻¹: 587 nm 3.6e3 (4K) / 8.2e2 (150K) / 2.3e2 (295K); 599 nm 4.2e4 / 1.4e4 / 5.6e2; 611 nm 9.3e4 / 5.2e4 / 5.0e3; 623/624 nm 1.1e3 / 3.1e3 / 1.8e4. The background rises toward high shift at 4 K 587 nm, consistent with an emission band near 1.95–2.05 eV.

observations.finding: The A1g−E2g separation Δ is the same at all three temperatures, within the scatter.

Δ ≈ 61 cm⁻¹ points to a monolayer-to-few-layer WS2 flake, not bulk. This is an inference that rests on the layer-dependent Δ in the literature and the assumption of 2H stacking. It does not give an exact layer number.
observations.evidence: Measured Δ = 60.9 ± 0.3 cm⁻¹ (see previous observation). Literature: Δ increases with layer number from about 61 cm⁻¹ (monolayer) to about 64 cm⁻¹ (bulk) (Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013); Zhao et al., Nanoscale 5, 9677 (2013); numbers from memory, verify).
observations.source: Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755 (2013); Zhao et al., Nanoscale 5, 9677 (2013) — from memory, verify exact values.

observations.finding: The absolute E2g and A1g positions carry an axis offset of 1–3 cm⁻¹ that depends on the run and on the laser setting. It is not a clean temperature effect, so absolute temperature coefficients cannot be extracted from these data.
observations.evidence: Si band positions co-shift with WS2 peaks between laser groups at fixed temperature. At 150 K, the 611/623 nm group relative to the 587/599 nm group: Si +2.9 cm⁻¹ (519.7/519.8 → 522.6/522.7), A1g +2.6 cm⁻¹ (417.2/417.0 → 419.7/419.8), E2g +2.5 cm⁻¹ (356.6/356.1 → 358.9/358.9). At 295 K, 610/624 nm vs 587/599 nm: Si +1.2, A1g +1.2, E2g +1.2 cm⁻¹. The 4 K group shows a similar but smaller co-shift.

observations.finding: The Si band at 295 K sits about 2.5 cm⁻¹ below the usual room-temperature reference, which indicates a systematic calibration offset in the 295 K set. Si at 4 K and 150 K is not ordered as expected for a temperature shift, so set-to-set offsets of order 1–2 cm⁻¹ remain unexplained.
observations.evidence: Well-constrained Si fits: 295 K 587.2 nm 517.87±0.04 cm⁻¹ (FWHM 5.0, rms 40 counts); 295 K 598.8 nm 518.39±0.06 (FWHM 4.5); 4 K 622.7 nm 521.71±0.02 (FWHM 3.4); 150 K 623.5 nm 522.71±0.02 (FWHM 3.0). Reference room-temperature Si ≈ 520.5–520.7 cm⁻¹ (common calibration value). Si temperature shift between 4 K and 295 K expected to be 1–2 cm⁻¹ (Balkanski et al., PRB 28, 1928 (1983), from memory, verify). Si fits at 4 K 587, 4 K 599, 150 K 599 and 4 K 611/150 K 611 have poor residuals or ~12 cm⁻¹ widths and were excluded.
observations.source: Reference Si value: common calibration (no specific paper verified); Balkanski et al., PRB 28, 1928 (1983), from memory.

observations.finding: The stated laser wavelengths for the same nominal dye setting differ between temperature sets by up to about 0.5–0.8 nm. Left uncorrected, that alone shifts Raman positions by ~14–22 cm⁻¹ at these wavelengths, so the laser metadata must be checked before the axes are trusted.
observations.evidence: Nominal 587 nm setting: 587.7 nm (4 K) vs 587.2 nm (150 K, 295 K). Nominal 623 nm setting: 622.66 nm (4 K) vs 623.48 nm (150 K) vs 623.97 nm (295 K). Sensitivity of Raman shift to laser wavelength: d(shift)/dλ = 1e7/λ² ≈ 29 cm⁻¹/nm at 587 nm and ≈ 26 cm⁻¹/nm at 623 nm.

observations.finding: The E2g and A1g linewidths are close to the instrument resolution and do not narrow on cooling. The A1g line is consistently wider than E2g.
observations.evidence: E2g FWHM (fit, 2-Lorentzian model): 3.2–4.2 cm⁻¹ at 4 K and 150 K, 3.3–4.1 cm⁻¹ at 295 K (587 nm at 295 K 6.0, low S/N). A1g FWHM: 5.2–7.6 cm⁻¹ at 4 K, 5.7–6.9 at 150 K, 6.0–7.1 at 295 K. Si FWHM 3.0–5.0 cm⁻¹ as an instrumental reference.

observations.finding: The sharp feature at about 146–147 cm⁻¹ is an edge artifact, not a phonon. The usable signal starts at a sharp step at 135–165 cm⁻¹ and ends at 630–710 cm⁻¹ (810 cm⁻¹ at 4 K 587 nm). Interlayer shear and breathing modes and LA(M) are therefore outside the usable window.
observations.evidence: The 146–147 cm⁻¹ maximum sits on the rising edge in 4 K 599/611/622, 150 K 611 and 295 K 624 nm (counts rise from ~10^2 to ~10^4–10^5 across the step). Low-shift step locations are approximately 160 cm⁻¹ (587 nm), 146 cm⁻¹ (599/611 nm) and 135 cm⁻¹ (623/624 nm). High-shift ends are approximately 710 (150 K and 295 K 587), 810 (4 K 587), 650–680 (599/611/598 nm) and 630 (622–624 nm). Reading from plots, ±10 cm⁻¹.

observations.finding: Several isolated single-channel spikes should be excluded from any fit or peak list.
observations.evidence: 295 K 587.2 nm at 758 cm⁻¹ (3733 counts); 295 K 624.0 nm at 36 cm⁻¹ (2038 counts); 150 K 587.2 nm at 186 cm⁻¹ (2031 counts). Each is a single-point spike with no neighbouring structure, consistent with cosmic rays or edge overshoot.

observations.finding: The E2g line overlaps a 2LA(M)-like component near 350–353 cm⁻¹. Its position and width are not stable enough to quantify temperature trends.
observations.evidence: Two-Lorentzian fits: second component at 350.8 (4K 587), 351.4 (4K 599), 352.9 (4K 611) cm⁻¹, with FWHM 4–13 cm⁻¹ and some fits poorly constrained at 295 K. E2g position from the narrower component: 356.75 (4K 587), 357.01 (4K 599), 357.34±0.22 (4K 611), 357.45 (4K 622).

observations.finding: The Si band intensity, which serves as an internal reference for throughput, varies by 2–4× between runs.
No LA(M)-region peak can be robustly identified near 173–178 cm⁻¹. A few spectra show a weak fitted feature, but it is only 2–10× the residual noise and sits on the steep edge and PL slope.
observations.evidence: Single-Lorentzian fit on a linear baseline over 165–205 cm⁻¹: fitted centres 173–178 cm⁻¹ in several spectra, but amplitude/rms 2–10 and sensitive to the baseline model.

observations.finding: There is no evidence for a magnetic, spin-related or strain-induced Raman signature in these data. WS2 is non-magnetic, so none is expected, and the Δ result shows no temperature-dependent strain or doping signature beyond the ±0.3 cm⁻¹ scatter. Δ is only a weak probe of strain and doping in WS2, so this is not a strong constraint.
observations.evidence: Δ constant within ±0.3 cm⁻¹ across 4–295 K (see Δ observation).
observations.source: Δ as a weak strain/doping probe: Rice et al., PRB 87, 081307(R) (2013) for MoS2 (from memory, verify).

caveats: Absolute phonon frequencies carry a run-dependent axis offset of about 1–3 cm⁻¹. The Si band co-shifts with the WS2 peaks at each laser setting. Do not quote temperature coefficients for E2g or A1g from these absolute positions.

The laser_nm labels are not consistent between temperature sets for the same nominal setting (587.7 vs 587.2 nm; 622.66 vs 623.48 nm). If the axis is computed from these labels, a 0.5 nm error gives about 14 cm⁻¹ at 587 nm.

Intensities are not on a common absolute scale across temperatures. They are affected by exciton resonance (the dominant effect), by a luminescence background that is 1–2 orders larger at 4 K, by a 2–4× variation in Si band intensity between runs, and possibly by a cryostat window or focus change. Only within-spectrum ratios and Δ are reasonably robust, and even A1g/E2g ratios are resonance-dependent (values range 1.8–11.8).

Local sample temperature is unknown. At 0.7 mW the flake on SiO2 in a cryostat may be heated well above the set-point, so the 4 K spectrum may not reflect 4 K. No power series was provided to assess this.

Background subtraction used a local quadratic baseline over each peak window. This is adequate for the A1g peak but less reliable for the E2g/2LA pair, which overlaps a broad component. Uncertainties on E2g areas are therefore larger than the statistical errors quoted.
Four laser energies per temperature, spaced 0.02–0.04 eV and mismatched by up to 1 nm between sets, sample the resonance coarsely. The resonance maxima are estimated to ±0.03 eV.
The window edge at about 135–165 cm⁻¹ and the high-shift cut at 630–810 cm⁻¹ differ between sets. Any fit or intensity comparison near these edges is affected.
The 295 K 587 nm spectrum is weak (A1g area ~5e3, E2g fit near noise), so its E2g position and A1g/E2g ratio are poorly determined (±0.3 cm⁻¹, ratio 1.8).
questions_for_user: Were the laser wavelengths measured with a wavemeter for each spectrum? The 4 K set is labelled 587.7 nm while the 150 K and 295 K sets are labelled 587.2 nm, and the 623 nm setting varies by about 1.3 nm between sets. Which value was used to build the Raman-shift axis?

How was the x-axis calibrated for each cool-down (for example neon/argon lamp, or Si at 520.7 cm⁻¹)? The Si band reads about 518 cm⁻¹ at 295 K and about 522 cm⁻¹ at 4 K/150 K, and the 295 K offset is about 2.5 cm⁻¹ from the usual reference.

Which edge or notch filter sets the low-shift cut at ~135–165 cm⁻¹, and what is its transmission? The 146–147 cm⁻¹ feature sits on that edge, so I treated it as an artifact. Is there any interlayer-mode data available from another setup or filter?
Is the spectral window cut at 630–810 cm⁻¹ from the CCD or grating position? It varies between runs at similar laser energy and affects background estimates near the high-shift edge.
Was a power series at 4 K (for example 0.07–0.7 mW) or a Stokes/anti-Stokes measurement made to estimate the laser-heated local temperature? Without it, the 4 K label is not verified for the sample.

Do you have an independent layer number for this flake (AFM step height, PL on the same spot, or a second Raman probe)? Δ ≈ 61 cm⁻¹ suggests monolayer-to-few-layer, but I cannot confirm the number from these data alone.
Were the cryostat window, objective and focus unchanged between temperature sets? The Si intensity differs by 2–4× between runs, which affects any absolute intensity comparison.

limits: No web access was available, so all literature values and citations are from memory and must be verified before use.
Only Stokes-side spectra are present, with no anti-Stokes, so local laser heating cannot be measured from these data.
No low-frequency (interlayer shear/breathing) modes and no reliable LA(M) are accessible because of the edge at ~135–165 cm⁻¹.
No defect-activated (D-type) features or doping markers were measured; defect level and doping type cannot be determined from these spectra.
Intensities are only corrected for spectrometer efficiency, and the Si band suggests residual throughput variation of 2–4×, so absolute cross-temperature intensity comparisons are not supported.
Laser conditions, power and the spot are taken as given (0.7 mW, same spot throughout). Power at the sample was not independently verified.
